extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (agents and attorneys), USPTO disciplinary personnel, and others involved in USPTO practitioner regulation
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, findings, and sanctions in a USPTO disciplinary Final Order addressing improper procurement of inventor oaths/declarations and related professional-conduct violations. Covers jurisdiction, violated rules, remedial/monitoring requirements, and enforcement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over practitioner disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26; practitioners are subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions are brought under the cited statutes and regulations; these provisions authorize the OED Director and USPTO Director to investigate, negotiate settlements, and impose sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that nonprovisional applications include a compliant oath/declaration (37 C.F.R. §§ 1.51(b)(2), 1.63)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional patent applications must include an oath or declaration by each inventor that complies with 37 C.F.R. § 1.63; the required § 1.63 oath/declaration must state that the person making it has reviewed and understands the contents of the application, including the claims, as amended by any amendment specifically referred to in the oath or declaration (see § 1.63(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An oath/declaration signed before the inventor has reviewed and understands the finished/complete application fails to satisfy § 1.63 and is contrary to patent prosecution rules; such noncompliance may cause harm to the client, the public, and the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining inventor oaths/declarations prior to inventor review of completed application
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not have inventor-clients sign the § 1.63 oath/declaration before the client has had the opportunity to review the completed specification, drawings, and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practice of obtaining signatures prior to preparation/completion of the application is 'plainly contrary' to patent prosecution rules and the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and is a basis for disciplinary action. Practitioners should offer clients the option to review the completed application before filing and signing the oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentation prohibition (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not engage in misrepresentation to the Office; conduct that amounts to misrepresentation violates § 10.23(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing, submitting, or causing to be filed papers that are false or misleading, or procuring signatures that do not reflect the signer's knowledge or assent, can constitute misrepresentation and support sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must avoid conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice; violating this prohibition is actionable under § 10.23(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices undermining the integrity of Office procedures (for example, obtaining declarations inconsistent with procedural rules) fall within this prohibition and may be disciplined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on signing papers in violation of § 11.18 (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(15))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must not sign a paper filed in the Office in violation of the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.18; violation of that prohibition is actionable under § 10.23(c)(15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing or causing to be filed papers when the signature or certification requirements of the governing rules are not met (e.g., oath/declaration requirements) can be a separate disciplinary violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: public reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose a public reprimand as an agreed-upon or ordered sanction for practitioner misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public reprimand will be published (e.g., Official Gazette and OED Reading Room) and becomes part of the practitioner's disciplinary record; it does not necessarily preclude continued practice subject to other terms (such as probation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: probation with conditions (36 months in this case)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose a probationary period (here, thirty-six months) during which the practitioner remains permitted to practice but is subject to conditions and oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation terms can include periodic reporting, monitoring, remedial actions, and the requirement to retain a practice monitor; failure to comply can trigger an Order to Show Cause and possible immediate suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause and immediate suspension process
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the practitioner failed to comply with the Final Order or disciplinary rules during probation, the OED Director will issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to the practitioner's address of record, and grant 15 days to respond; if noncompliance remains, the OED Director may request the USPTO Director to enter an order immediately suspending the practitioner for up to 24 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After issuing the Order to Show Cause and considering any response, the OED Director prepares supporting argument and evidence to deliver to the USPTO Director to request immediate suspension; if suspension is entered, review by the practitioner does not stay the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of immediate suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director enters an order immediately suspending the practitioner, the USPTO will promptly dissociate the practitioner's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates, and the practitioner may not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate suspension results in loss of access/associations used for electronic filing and representation, and reinstatement procedures are required before resuming practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and publish a materially consistent notice in the Official Gazette describing the practitioner's sanction and the facts supporting it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication serves notice to the public and other stakeholders and memorializes the practitioner’s misconduct and discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required remedial actions and affidavit reporting schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must take remedial action communicated between the parties within 180 days and provide affidavits attesting to remedial action at specified intervals: within 75 days, within 135 days (not inclusive of the first 75 days), and within 195 days (not inclusive of the first 135 days) from the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits must attest to the remedial action taken to date at each reporting interval, providing staged documentation of correction efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice monitor requirement and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must hire, at his expense, a practice monitor who is an attorney registered to practice before the Office and licensed/in good standing in California; the practice monitor must regularly review Respondent's patent practice during probation and submit reports to the OED Director every six months for the 36-month probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each six-month report must state whether Respondent is in compliance with patent prosecution rules (regulatory and statutory), and if not, identify each implicated patent prosecution rule and briefly explain how Respondent's acts or omissions fail to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation of OED's right to pursue further discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from seeking discipline under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34–11.57 for the misconduct that led to immediate suspension, nor from considering the record of this proceeding in future disciplinary matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may use the record of this proceeding as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by or on behalf of the practitioner in any future disciplinary proceeding; settlement does not preclude additional action if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on pending proceedings and motions
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall file a motion to dismiss the currently pending disciplinary proceeding against Respondent within thirty (30) days of the Final Order being signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement terms may include dismissal of pending matters contingent on compliance with the Agreement and Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party (the OED Director and Respondent) bears their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement specified that neither side recovers costs from the other as part of the resolution.
